# A handler inside a view loop reads the loop's own variable, on bubbletea.
#
# Every head form a focusable loop can take is here, because the focus cursor
# is an int ordinal and each head answers "which iteration is this?"
# differently -- a map head cannot answer at all and needs a counter (#174).
#
# Which of the two loop variables the handler reads varies from loop to loop,
# and Go rejects the one it does not. On a map head the ordinal is a counter
# rather than the key, so either position can now go unread. The unread names
# here are ones the rendered body happens to spell inside another word --
# `k` and `it` inside `picked` and `hits` -- which is what a substring test
# over the rendered Go cannot tell from a reference.
#
# This has to be a compiled run: the interpreter never emits either loop, so
# `--platform none` passes under the bug.
#
# The bool-keyed map is the key type Go will not order for us: it compiles only
# if the ordered walk has a comparator to fall back on.

[!exec:go] skip 'go toolchain required'

sngl test --platform=bubbletea --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'PASS'

-- app.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import . "sngl:test"

output { go { bubbletea } }

component main {
    var items list<string> = ["a", "b"]
    var labels map<string, string> = {a = "A", b = "B"}
    var flags map<bool, string> = {true = "on", false = "off"}
    var picked = ""
    var hits = 0

    vbox {
        for var it = items {
            button(text=it, @click { picked = it })
        }
        for items {
            button(text="any", @click { hits += 1 })
        }
        for var i, it = items {
            button(text=it, @click { picked = "{i}:{it}" })
        }
        for var k, v = labels {
            button(text=v, @click { picked = k })
        }
        for var k, v = labels {
            button(text=v, @click { picked = v })
        }
        for var k, v = labels {
            button(text=v, @click { picked = "" })
        }
        for labels {
            button(text="any", @click { hits += 1 })
        }
        for var i, it = items {
            button(text=it, @click { hits += i })
        }
        for var f, fv = flags {
            button(text=fv, @click { picked = fv })
        }
    }
    text(value=picked)
}

func testStartsEmpty(t Test, c main) {
    t.assert(c.picked == "")
    t.assert(c.hits == 0)
}
